- [`devkit ci pac`](#devkit-ci-pac) — Wire GitHub webhooks into the Kind cluster: a smee channel of your own for the gitops gosmee client, and the GitHub App Secret PaC authenticates with.
- [`devkit ci run`](#devkit-ci-run) — Resolve one .tekton/ PipelineRun as Pipelines-as-Code would, and run it on the Kind cluster against a pushed commit. The clone credential is a Secret holding your gh token, owned by the PipelineRun, so Kubernetes deletes it with the run.

- [`devkit cluster deps`](#devkit-cluster-deps) — Install cluster dependencies declared in config `[[deps]]`. Helm rows: { name, repo, chart?, version?, namespace?, timeout?, values?, set?, depends_on? } — chart defaults to name, namespace to "default", timeout to "10m"; omit repo to use chart as a full reference (e.g. oci://...). `values` is a values file path or list of paths (helm -f, later files win), resolved against $PWD then the devkit.toml directory; a missing file is a hard error. `set` is a key=value string or list of them (helm --set, wins over values files). Manifest rows: { name, manifest, depends_on? } are applied with kubectl --server-side (URL or repo-relative path; SSA handles large CRDs). `depends_on` is a dep name or list of names that must be installed first — use it when a dep needs another dep's CRDs/webhooks/controllers. Deps are grouped into levels (see deps-levels): a level installs in PARALLEL and only starts after the previous level fully succeeded. `flux_depends_on` (Flux Kustomization names) moves a row after Flux: plain `deps` skips it, `deps --after-flux` waits for those Kustomizations to be Ready (flux.wait_timeout) and installs only such rows. `devkit up --flux` runs both phases around the Flux install. Command output is captured per dep and only shown on failure. Idempotent.

- [`devkit setup bench`](#devkit-setup-bench) — Measure every available build strategy on this Cargo workspace (cold, no-op, incremental, rebuild-after-clean) in throwaway target dirs and caches, print the table, and save the pick for this workspace. `setup build/check/test` then use the picked strategy here. Your target dir and compiler caches are not touched; one workspace source file gets its mtime bumped for the incremental scenario.
- [`devkit setup build`](#devkit-setup-build) — Build all Rust packages
- [`devkit setup check`](#devkit-setup-check) — Run quality checks
- [`devkit setup install`](#devkit-setup-install) — Install system dependencies. Tools already on PATH are skipped with a lookup; only missing ones reach brew/cargo/apt.
- [`devkit setup test`](#devkit-setup-test) — Run tests
- [`devkit setup vault-setup`](#devkit-setup-vault-setup) — Setup Vault secrets structure
- [`devkit status`](#devkit-status) — Show environment status
- [`devkit up`](#devkit-up) — Bring up the local development environment. Extras are opt-in via flags: --istio, --core, --gitops, --observability, --flux. Ingress is always enabled.

## `devkit`

Overview of the most-used commands. Run a group (e.g. `devkit cluster`) to list
its subcommands, or `help devkit <cmd>` for details on any command.

```nu
devkit
```

## `devkit ci`

Tekton PipelineRuns on the local Kind cluster. Run a subcommand, or `help devkit ci <cmd>`.

```nu
devkit ci
```

## `devkit ci list`

PipelineRuns in the repo's .tekton/, with what each builds.

```nu
devkit ci list
```

## `devkit ci pac`

Wire GitHub webhooks into the Kind cluster: a smee channel of your own for the
gitops gosmee client, and the GitHub App Secret PaC authenticates with.

The gitops tree commits a placeholder channel (PAC_SMEE_URL in the local
cluster-config), because a channel URL can read every payload sent to it.
This command marks the gosmee Deployment as Flux-unreconciled on this cluster
and points it at your channel. The rest of the tree still reconciles.

Register the local GitHub App once, with your channel as its webhook URL
(gitops README, "CI: Tekton" > Prerequisites: permissions and events), install
it on the repositories, then pass its credentials here.

```nu
devkit ci pac {flags}
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--name`, `-n` | string |  | Kind cluster name (default: config cluster.name) |
| `--smee-url` | string |  | Channel to use and save (default: the saved one, else a new one) |
| `--app-id` | int |  | GitHub App id; with --private-key and --webhook-secret, (re)create the App Secret |
| `--private-key` | path |  | The App's PEM private key file |
| `--webhook-secret` | string |  | The App's webhook secret (PaC checks every payload's HMAC with it) |

## `devkit ci run`

Resolve one .tekton/ PipelineRun as Pipelines-as-Code would, and run it on the
Kind cluster against a pushed commit. The clone credential is a Secret holding
your gh token, owned by the PipelineRun, so Kubernetes deletes it with the run.

```nu
devkit ci run {flags} <pipelinerun>
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pipelinerun` | string |  | File stem under [ci].dir (see `devkit ci list`) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--revision`, `-r` | string |  | Commit to build (default: the upstream of HEAD); must be on GitHub |
| `--name`, `-n` | string |  | Kind cluster name (default: config cluster.name) |
| `--follow`, `-f` | switch |  | Stream the logs and fail when the run fails |
| `--dry-run` | switch |  | Print the resolved PipelineRun instead of creating it |

## `devkit ci status`

PaC's view of the repository and its latest runs, and whether webhooks can
reach the Kind cluster: the App Secret, and gosmee's channel.

```nu
devkit ci status {flags}
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--name`, `-n` | string |  | Kind cluster name (default: config cluster.name) |

## `devkit cluster deps`

Install cluster dependencies declared in config `[[deps]]`.
Helm rows: { name, repo, chart?, version?, namespace?, timeout?, values?, set?, depends_on? } —
chart defaults to name, namespace to "default", timeout to "10m"; omit repo
to use chart as a full reference (e.g. oci://...). `values` is a values file
path or list of paths (helm -f, later files win), resolved against $PWD then
the devkit.toml directory; a missing file is a hard error. `set` is a
key=value string or list of them (helm --set, wins over values files).
Manifest rows: { name, manifest, depends_on? } are applied with kubectl
--server-side (URL or repo-relative path; SSA handles large CRDs).
`depends_on` is a dep name or list of names that must be installed first —
use it when a dep needs another dep's CRDs/webhooks/controllers. Deps are
grouped into levels (see deps-levels): a level installs in PARALLEL and only
starts after the previous level fully succeeded.
`flux_depends_on` (Flux Kustomization names) moves a row after Flux: plain
`deps` skips it, `deps --after-flux` waits for those Kustomizations to be
Ready (flux.wait_timeout) and installs only such rows. `devkit up --flux`
runs both phases around the Flux install.
Command output is captured per dep and only shown on failure. Idempotent.

```nu
devkit cluster deps {flags}
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--after-flux` | switch |  | Install only the rows with flux_depends_on, once those Kustomizations are Ready |

## `devkit cluster oidc`

Re-render the [cluster.oidc] AuthenticationConfiguration of a running Kind
cluster, e.g. once ca_file exists (a CA minted in-cluster after create) or
after changing a claim, prefix or audience. kube-apiserver reloads the file
within about a minute, without a restart; an invalid file is logged by the
apiserver and the previous config stays active. Only works on clusters
created with [cluster.oidc] set: the mount and the flag are create-time.

```nu
devkit cluster oidc {flags}
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--name`, `-n` | string |  | Cluster name (default: config cluster.name) |

## `devkit cluster setup`

Post-cluster setup - deploy common infrastructure

```nu
devkit cluster setup {flags}
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--flux` | switch |  | Install Flux via the Flux Operator (+ Web UI) |
| `--flux-repo` | string |  | Flux repository (default: config flux.repository) |
| `--flux-owner` | string |  | GitHub owner/org (default: config flux.owner, else gh user) |
| `--keep-flux-bootstrap` | switch |  | Keep `<sync path>/flux-system/` in the repo (skip migration cleanup) |
| `--istio` | switch |  | Install Istio |
| `--dbs` | switch |  | Deploy database services from compose |
| `--external-secrets` | switch |  | Install ESO + GCP credentials + ClusterSecretStore |

## `devkit config`

Show the effective config (DEFAULTS deep-merged with the discovered devkit.toml).
Nested records/tables are expanded so every value is visible; use --data for a
raw record you can pipe (e.g. `devkit config --data | get cluster.name`).

```nu
devkit config {flags}
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--file`, `-f` | string |  | explicit config file path |
| `--path` | switch |  | only print the resolved config file path |
| `--data` | switch |  | output the raw record for piping instead of a table |

## `devkit config init`

Scaffold a devkit.toml from the bundled reference into the target directory.

```nu
devkit config init {flags} [dir]
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | string |  | Target directory (default: git repo root, else $PWD) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--force` | switch |  | Overwrite an existing devkit.toml |

## `devkit config search`

Find every devkit.toml under a directory (default: $HOME, i.e. the whole
machine). Unlike `find-config-file` (walks up from $PWD to the nearest one),
this walks down a tree to list every repo devkit already knows about.

```nu
devkit config search {flags} [dir]
```

Input/output: `nothing -> list<string>`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | string |  | Directory to search (default: $HOME) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--depth` | int |  | Limit recursion depth (default: unlimited) |
| `--all` | switch |  | Don't skip node_modules/.git/target/Library/... (slow) |

CustomResourceDefinitions as tables. Run a subcommand, or `help devkit crd <cmd>`.

## `devkit crd fields`

One row per field of every CRD version, depth first. Paths mark array items
with `[]` and map values with `.*` (`spec.containers[].env.*`).

```nu
devkit crd fields {flags} [file]
```

Input/output: `any -> table`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | path |  | YAML/JSON file holding the CRDs (default: piped input) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--kind`, `-k` | string |  | Only this kind (spec.names.kind, case-insensitive) |
| `--version`, `-v` | string |  | Only this version (default: every version) |

## `devkit crd list`

One row per CRD: kind, name, group, scope, versions (`*` marks the storage


Input/output: `any -> table`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | path |  | YAML/JSON file holding the CRDs (default: piped input) |

## `devkit secrets`

vals / vault secret handling. Run a subcommand, or `help devkit secrets <cmd>`.

```nu
devkit secrets
```

## `devkit secrets fetch`

Fetch secrets using vals and generate a .env file.

Refs are resolved via `vals eval` (structured), not `vals env`, so multi-line
and JSON values survive intact. Secrets that resolve to a JSON object are
recursively flattened into individual KEY=VALUE lines: nested field names are
joined with '_' and the parent secret name is NOT used as a prefix (e.g.
APP_SECRETS.github.token -> GITHUB_TOKEN). Scalars pass through unchanged.
Duplicate keys collapse to the first occurrence; a warning is emitted only if
their values actually differ. Use --no-flatten to keep each object as a single
JSON-valued variable under its own name.

```nu
devkit secrets fetch {flags}
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--output`, `-o` | string | `""` | Output file path (defaults to config secrets.output) |
| `--config`, `-c` | string | `""` | vals config file (defaults to config secrets.config) |
| `--no-flatten` | switch |  | Keep JSON-object secrets as one JSON-valued var |

## `devkit secrets list`


| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--config`, `-c` | string | `""` | vals config file (defaults to config secrets.config) |

## `devkit setup`

Toolchain install, build, check, test. Run a subcommand, or `help devkit setup <cmd>`.

```nu
devkit setup
```

## `devkit setup all`

Full setup: install everything, then one dev build of every target so the
next `setup build` / `setup test` is incremental. --release builds shippable
binaries instead: ~3x slower cold, and nothing in the dev loop reuses them.

```nu
devkit setup all {flags}
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--release`, `-r` | switch |  | Release build instead of the dev --all-targets build |

## `devkit setup bench`

Measure every available build strategy on this Cargo workspace (cold,
no-op, incremental, rebuild-after-clean) in throwaway target dirs and
caches, print the table, and save the pick for this workspace. `setup
build/check/test` then use the picked strategy here. Your target dir and
compiler caches are not touched; one workspace source file gets its mtime
bumped for the incremental scenario.

```nu
devkit setup bench {flags}
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--runs`, `-n` | int | `1` | Repetitions per strategy (median per scenario) |
| `--no-save` | switch |  | Print only; do not store the pick |

## `devkit setup build`

Build all Rust packages

```nu
devkit setup build {flags}
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--release`, `-r` | switch |  | Build in release mode |
| `--app`, `-a` | string |  | Build specific app |
| `--all-targets`, `-t` | switch |  | Also build tests/examples/benches (makes the next `setup test` incremental) |

| `--k8s` | switch |  | Install Kubernetes tools |
| `--all`, `-a` | switch |  | Install everything |

## `devkit up`

Bring up the local development environment. Extras are opt-in via flags:
--istio, --core, --gitops, --observability, --flux. Ingress is always enabled.

```nu
devkit up {flags}
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--name`, `-n` | string |  | Cluster name (default: config cluster.name) |
| `--workers`, `-w` | int | `-1` | Worker nodes (default: config cluster.workers) |
| `--skip-dbs` | switch |  | Skip database deployment |
| `--skip-secrets` | switch |  | Skip external-secrets setup |
| `--skip-tilt` | switch |  | Skip starting Tilt |
| `--istio` | switch |  | Install Istio (ambient) before workloads |
| `--core` | switch |  | Apply the core infrastructure overlay |
| `--gitops` | switch |  | Apply the GitOps overlay |
| `--observability` | switch |  | Deploy the observability stack |
| `--flux` | switch |  | Install Flux via the Flux Operator (+ Web UI) |
| `--dry-run` | switch |  | Preview without executing |
| `--verbose`, `-v` | switch |  | Verbose output |
